claim: gRFC A6 'gRPC Retry Design' by Noah Eisen and Eric Gribkoff is implemented (Java, .NET, Node; Go and C-Core without hedging) and was last updated 2024-08-23.
quote: Status: Implemented * Implemented in: Java, .NET, Node, Go except hedging, and C-Core except hedging * Last updated: 2024-08-23
source: A6: gRPC Retry Design, Noah Eisen and Eric Gribkoff, grpc/proposal
note: Fetched as raw markdown from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/grpc/proposal/master/A6-client-retries.md; '*' marks list bullets.

claim: A retryPolicy has maxAttempts, initialBackoff, maxBackoff, backoffMultiplier and retryableStatusCodes; the gRFC example uses 4 attempts, 0.1 s initial, 1 s max, multiplier 2, retrying UNAVAILABLE.
quote: "maxAttempts": 4, "initialBackoff": "0.1s", "maxBackoff": "1s", "backoffMultiplier": 2, "retryableStatusCodes": [ "UNAVAILABLE" ]
source: A6: gRPC Retry Design, Noah Eisen and Eric Gribkoff, grpc/proposal
note: JSON example with line breaks collapsed. Field definition: 'maxAttempts specifies the maximum number of RPC attempts, including the original request.'

claim: gRPC applies plus or minus 20% jitter: the n-th attempt waits min(initialBackoff*backoffMultiplier**(n-1), maxBackoff) * random(0.8, 1.2).
quote: After that, the n-th attempt will occur after min(initialBackoff*backoffMultiplier**(n-1), maxBackoff) * random(0.8, 1.2)).
source: A6: gRPC Retry Design, Noah Eisen and Eric Gribkoff, grpc/proposal
note: Backticks dropped; the unbalanced closing parenthesis is in the source. Preceding: 'The initial retry attempt will occur after initialBackoff * random(0.8, 1.2).' and 'Jitter of plus or minus 0.2 is applied to the backoff delay'.

claim: maxAttempts must be greater than 1, and values above 5 are silently treated as 5 (a client-side maximum changeable via channel arguments).
quote: maxAttempts MUST be specified and MUST be a JSON integer value greater than 1. Values greater than 5 are treated as 5 without being considered a validation error.
source: A6: gRPC Retry Design, Noah Eisen and Eric Gribkoff, grpc/proposal
note: Backticks dropped. Also: 'maxAttempts in both retryPolicy and hedgingPolicy have, by default, a client-side maximum value of 5.'

claim: retryableStatusCodes must be a non-empty list of valid gRPC status codes, given as integers or names.
quote: retryableStatusCodes MUST be specified as a JSON array of status codes and be non-empty.
source: A6: gRPC Retry Design, Noah Eisen and Eric Gribkoff, grpc/proposal

claim: Retry throttling is configured per server name with maxTokens and tokenRatio (example 10 and 0.1); maxTokens must be in (0, 1000].
quote: gRPC prevents server overload due to retries and hedged RPCs by disabling these policies when the client's ratio of failures to successes passes a certain threshold. The throttling is done per server name.
source: A6: gRPC Retry Design, Noah Eisen and Eric Gribkoff, grpc/proposal
note: Curly apostrophe normalised. Example: "retryThrottling": { "maxTokens": 10, "tokenRatio": 0.1 }. Validation: 'maxTokens MUST be specified and MUST be a JSON integer value in the range (0, 1000].'

claim: token_count starts at maxTokens; each failed RPC subtracts 1, each success adds tokenRatio, and retries (and extra hedges) stop while token_count is at or below maxTokens/2.
quote: If token_count is less than or equal to the threshold, defined to be (maxTokens / 2), then RPCs will not be retried until token_count rises over the threshold.
source: A6: gRPC Retry Design, Noah Eisen and Eric Gribkoff, grpc/proposal
note: Backticks dropped. Also: 'Every failed RPC will decrement the token_count by 1.' and 'Every successful RPC will increment the token_count by tokenRatio.' Only retryable or non-fatal status codes (or a do-not-retry pushback) count as failures.

claim: A hedgingPolicy sends the original RPC at once and another copy every hedgingDelay without a successful response, up to maxAttempts; the call deadline covers the whole chain.
quote: After hedgingDelay has elapsed without a successful response, the second RPC will be issued. If neither RPC has received a response after hedgingDelay has elapsed again, a third RPC is sent, and so on, up to maxAttempts.
source: A6: gRPC Retry Design, Noah Eisen and Eric Gribkoff, grpc/proposal
note: Backticks dropped. Example config: maxAttempts 4, hedgingDelay 0.5s. Also: 'As with retries, gRPC call deadlines apply to the entire chain of hedged requests.'

claim: Once the response headers arrive the RPC is committed and gRPC makes no further retries.
quote: Once the response header is received, the RPC is committed. No further retries will be attempted, and gRPC hands over the RPC to the application.

claim: gRPC enables retries by default but ships no default retry policy; without one only transparent retries of unprocessed RPCs happen.
quote: Retries are enabled by default, but there is no default retry policy. Without a retry policy, gRPC cannot safely retry RPCs in most cases.

claim: The gRPC guide summarises throttling: retries pause when token_count falls below half of maxTokens; with initialBackoff 100 ms the first retry waits 80 to 120 ms.
quote: Failed RPCs decrement the count by 1, successful RPCs increment it by tokenRatio. If the token_count falls below half of maxTokens, retries are paused until the count recovers.
note: The guide says 'falls below half'; the gRFC says 'less than or equal to'. Also: 'initialBackoff is set to 100ms, so the actual backoff delay after the first attempt will be for a random time period within the range [80ms, 120ms].'

claim: gRPC sets no deadline by default, so clients should always set one explicitly.
quote: By default, gRPC does not set a deadline which means it is possible for a client to end up waiting for a response effectively forever.
note: Next: 'To avoid this you should always explicitly set a realistic deadline in your clients.'

claim: Some gRPC implementations propagate a server's incoming deadline to its outgoing calls (on by default in Java and Go, opt-in in C++), converting it to a remaining timeout to avoid clock skew.
quote: Automatically propagating the deadline from an incoming RPC to an outgoing one is supported by some gRPC implementations. In some languages this behavior needs to be explicitly enabled (e.g. C++) and in others it is enabled by default (e.g. Java and Go).
note: Also: 'To address this gRPC converts the deadline to a timeout from which the already elapsed time is already deducted.'

claim: Finagle's default RetryBudget allows about 20% of requests to be retried on top of 10 retries per second.
quote: By default, the RetryBudget allows for about 20% of the total requests to be immediately (no backoff) retried on top of 10 retries per second
note: Continues: 'in order to accommodate clients that have just started issuing requests or clients that have a low rate of requests per second.' The parameters are ttl ('a time to live for deposited tokens'), minRetriesPerSec and percentCanRetry; it is backed by a leaky token bucket.

claim: In Finagle's source the default RetryBudget uses ttl 10 seconds, minRetriesPerSec 10 and percentCanRetry 0.2.
quote: private[finagle] val DefaultTtl = 10.seconds / private[finagle] val DefaultMinRetriesPerSec = 10 / apply(DefaultTtl, DefaultMinRetriesPerSec, 0.2, Stopwatch.systemMillis)
note: ' / ' separates source lines (97, 99, 114). ttl must be between 1 and 60 seconds; 'if 0.1 is used, then for every 10 calls to deposit(), 1 retry will be allowed.'

claim: Envoy's cluster RetryBudget limits concurrent retries to budget_percent of active plus pending requests, default 20%.
quote: Specifies the limit on concurrent retries as a percentage of the sum of active requests and active pending requests.
note: Same field: 'This parameter is optional. Defaults to 20%.' Example: '100 active requests and the budget_percent is set to 25, there may be 25 active retries.'

claim: Envoy's retry budget never allows fewer than min_retry_concurrency active retries, default 3; a set retry budget overrides the max_retries circuit breaker (default 3 parallel retries).
quote: Specifies the minimum retry concurrency allowed for the retry budget. The limit on the number of active retries may never go below this number. This parameter is optional. Defaults to 3.
note: Also: 'If this field is set, the retry budget will override any configured retry circuit breaker.' and max_retries: 'If not specified, the default is 3.'

claim: Envoy's route RetryPolicy num_retries defaults to 1.
quote: Specifies the allowed number of retries. This parameter is optional and defaults to 1.

claim: Envoy's default retry backoff base is 25 ms and the default maximum interval is 10 times the base.
quote: the default base interval is 25 milliseconds or, if set, the current value of the upstream.base_retry_backoff_ms runtime parameter. The default maximum interval is 10 times the base interval.
source: Route components (proto), config.route.v3.RetryPolicy retry_back_off, Envoy documentation

claim: Envoy uses fully jittered exponential backoff: retry N waits a random time in [0, (2^N - 1)B), i.e. 0-24 ms, 0-74 ms, 0-174 ms with B = 25 ms, capped at 250 ms by default.
quote: By default, Envoy uses a fully jittered exponential back-off algorithm for retries with a default base interval of 25ms.
note: Also: 'the first retry will be delayed randomly by 0-24ms, the 2nd by 0-74ms, the 3rd by 0-174ms' and 'The interval is capped at a maximum interval, which defaults to 10 times the base interval (250ms).' The range is rendered as LaTeX [0, (2^N-1)B).

claim: Envoy's route timeout covers all retries, so retries share one overall budget instead of multiplying timeouts.
quote: This is by design to avoid an exponential retry/timeout explosion.
note: Preceding: 'if the request timeout is set to 3s, and the first request attempt takes 2.7s, the retry (including back-off) has .3s to complete.'
